context: In 0-1 knapsack, take each item at most once and maximize the total value without exceeding the capacity. Here there are 5 items and cap=50. The figure numbers items i from 1 through 5, corresponding to array index i-1 (the original column headers read wgt[i-1] and val[i-1]).
description: The upper-left table lists icons, weights, and values for items 1–5 (see the table for all data). The banana row, item 2, has a light orange background, and the grapes row, item 3, has a light purple background. An arrow from each leads to the purple knapsack at the upper right, labeled “Knapsack capacity cap = 50.”
The result box below reads “Maximum value: 270.” Banana and grape icons accompany the explanation “Optimal choice: pack the banana and grapes, using 50 units of capacity.”

frames.explanation: From the input, the banana (2) and grapes (3) weigh 20+30=50 and are worth 120+150=270. This is the highest value among all combinations that fit. For comparison, items 1 and 4 give 260, while item 5 alone gives 240. These calculations and comparisons are derived from the figure's input.
frames.title: 0-1 knapsack: optimal choice for capacity 50

summary: Of five items, choose the banana weighing 20 and the grapes weighing 30. They exactly fill capacity 50 and achieve the maximum value of 270.
